summary: Intermittent long-tail latency in structured-output mode when model emits large enumerations
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 10-30s tail latency spikes and occasional 504s when using structured_output mode for tasks that emit long arrays (thousands of items). Impact: Production search-indexing pipeline using our hosted API experienced several failed requests and delayed downstream processing. Environment: prod us-east, requests via hosted API, structured_output=true, streaming disabled.

Observed behavior: Most requests complete sub-500ms, but ~1-2% of calls for large enumerations spike to >10s and sometimes time out. Spikes appear correlated with the model producing very long JSON arrays and payloads with many comma-separated items.

Expected behavior: Structured output decoding should not add long-tail latency; streaming responses or chunked parsing should emit tokens progressively and complete within normal percentiles.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use hosted API endpoint with structured_output=true and streaming=false
2) Prompt the model to generate a JSON array of ~3000 short items (e.g., list of normalized entity objects)
3) Observe latency distribution over 500+ requests; identify 95/99/999p spikes
4) Re-run with streaming=true and compare latencies
5) Repeat with alternative models (redwood/chat-3b and openlm-llama-13b)
Notes: customer provided a sample prompt and corpus attached to initial support attachment (not stored here)
logs: Proxy logs show upstream 200 from runtime at t=360ms, but response assembly held until t=11.2s for req-0375f
Runtime trace: parser buffer flush at offset 0x1f48 took 10.8s in parse_json_chunk()
Gateway reported backpressure spikes and repeated zero-byte writes to client socket before final flush
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer says problem started after last runtime deploy (2026-03-08). They only see issues when the model produces very long flat arrays.

Luis Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with redwood/chat-3b. Initial hypothesis: incremental parser uses an internal boundary heuristic that defers buffer emission for comma-delimited sequences, causing blocking until a final close-bracket or flush is seen.

Aisha Patel (Eng - parser) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed parser path parse_json_chunk() uses a 'lookahead' that can wait for up to 8k tokens before emitting; this interacts poorly with streaming=false and large enumerations. Adding instrumentation to measure wait times.
Customer (MapleDocs) - 2026-03-12: Provided 12 sample prompts and 90 failing request IDs. Impact: indexing job fell behind SLA by 3 hours for one batch.

Luis Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Temporary mitigation suggested for customer: set structured_output_chunk_threshold=1024 OR enable streaming=true. Customer validated streaming=true reduces spikes but changes client-side handling.
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-13: Will coordinate final patch rollout and schedule customer-facing communication about config option and timeline.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Parser 'enumeration lookahead' heuristic waits for additional tokens to decide whether to emit a partial array item, causing delays when items are small and numerous.
Hypothesis 2: Gateway backpressure + runtime write coalescing leads to delayed flush when response body is primarily commas and braces (small tokens), exacerbated by streaming=false path.
Repro steps executed in staging: crafted PR that toggles lookahead to 256 tokens; median latency unchanged but 99.9p improved from 12.1s -> 0.9s in local test (3000-item array).
Perf trace: CPU usage steady; blocking is in parser IO path waiting on internal condition variable (cv) in parse_json_chunk().
Related signals: increase in socket write vfs_queue length for affected requests; no OOMs observed.
Cross-reference: See SUP-17821 for related final-chunk blocking behavior on structured output when unicode escapes are present.

Action items: create a small runtime hotfix to lower lookahead threshold and add an adaptive flush when array length > 512; add e2e test with large enumerations; add monitoring alert for parser_hang_seconds>2.
resolution: Workaround provided: customer set streaming=true for affected endpoints which eliminated the >10s spikes for their workload. Alternatively, set structured_output_chunk_threshold=1024 on request-level config to force earlier flush.

Fix implemented: PR #842 shortens enumeration lookahead to 256 tokens and adds an adaptive flush when array item count exceeds threshold. Test coverage added for long enumeration streaming and non-streaming paths.
Rollout plan: Canary rollout to 5% traffic in us-east on 2026-03-14, monitor 99.9p latency and socket queues. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-16 pending no regressions.
Follow-ups: Update structured-output runbook with config knobs; add documented guidance in SDK docs about streaming vs structured_output tradeoffs; postmortem planned if customer sees further impact.
Status: Patch merged to main; canary deployed. Pending verification from customer that batch indexing recovered.
